title: Before the Silence
description: Music, friendship and an ordinary life give way to exhaustion, persistent pain and a search for somewhere to belong.

readerPages.text:
THE FIRST CHAPTER




BEFORE THE
SILENCE
Before A Moment of Quiet

This was home                                                       THE STORY



   Before the forms, the building sites and the pain, there was
   music.




   One more?                            Please. I love hearing you
                                        play.




   His lover. His friends. The people he called family. In Spain,
   he had a life.




BEFORE THE SILENCE                                                         2

A life in rhythm                                                  THE STORY



   Rehearsal. Work. Coffee with friends. Several languages,
   moving easily between them. A daily rhythm that belonged
   to him.




   Music was his craft, his career and a way to belong. He
   wanted to keep building that life.




   From the UK, he heard far-right nationalism: borders, blame,
   promises to take something back.




BEFORE THE SILENCE                                                       3

A decision over their lives                                    THE STORY



   23 June 2016: the UK votes to leave the EU. He had wanted
   to remain part of it.




   Some British citizens
   abroad were excluded
   by the 15-year voting
   rule. A decision over
   their lives, without their
   voices.




   I fear they see me as the           I know you. You are still my
   hatred I reject.                    friend.




BEFORE THE SILENCE                                                    4

The life he could not keep                                            THE STORY



   The money. The manipulation. Russia. Who is
   answering these questions?




   His work. His band. His relationship. The daily rhythm of
   home. To him, Brexit had taken his freedom.




                                              He returned to the UK
                                              against his will. The life he
                                              wanted was behind him.




BEFORE THE SILENCE                                                            5

The only door that opened                                         THE STORY



   He spoke several languages. He had multiple degrees. The
   work he could actually get was on building sites.




                                     Lift. Carry. Keep going. Work he
                                     never wanted, because he could
                                     not find an affordable way out.




   Hands aching. Guitar closed. Tomorrow already owed.




BEFORE THE SILENCE                                                       6

Again. And again.                                              THE STORY



   Wake. Dress. Go. Another early start. Another day to get
   through.




   Years pass. The sites change.
   The weight does not.




                                      “Forced manual labour.
                                      Slavery.”


                     “All this work. Not
                     enough to live on.
                     Nothing to live for.”




BEFORE THE SILENCE                                                    7

No peace in the work                                               THE STORY



   The racist jokes. The drinking. The casual cruelty. He heard
   contempt for people he loved.




                                    He wanted a wage without hatred. A
                                    conversation without humiliation.
                                    Somewhere his mind could breathe.




   A different site. For a little
   while, he thought he had
   escaped it.




BEFORE THE SILENCE                                                        8

The visitor                                                          THE STORY



   At the new site, a familiar visitor appeared: gun
   photographs, talk of violence. To him, a fascist fantasy.




                                        “I came here to work. Why
                                        must I keep living inside
                                        someone else's hatred?”




                                        He kept going. Until one day, he
                                        could not.




BEFORE THE SILENCE                                                          9

When his body gave way                                                THE STORY



   A collapse. He would later describe a seizure, spinal
   compression and loss of motor control.




   He thought he was dying. In that exhaustion,
   part of him hoped it was the end.




   Stay with me. Help is here.




                                          He needed care. Safety. A
                                          chance to live.


BEFORE THE SILENCE                                                          10

The history around the story                                         CONTEXT & SOURCES




 A personal account can show what political change feels like inside one life. These
 notes distinguish the historical record from the character's judgments and the
 fictional staging.
 A lawful referendum, with an advisory legal effect
 The 23 June 2016 referendum was authorised by the European Union Referendum
 Act 2015: a real ballot, not an illegal opinion poll. Leave received 51.9% of valid
 votes; Remain 48.1%. The Act did not itself change the law after the result.
 Parliament subsequently authorised Article 50 notification in 2017 and passed
 withdrawal legislation. An advisory effect did not create an automatic right to a
 second referendum. [1, 2, 3]
 Whose voices were missing?
 The 2016 franchise excluded some British citizens abroad under the then 15-year
 overseas-voting limit. Most other EU citizens living in the UK were also excluded,
 with specified exceptions. It is accurate to question those exclusions; it is not
 accurate to say everyone who favoured Remain was denied a vote. The story does
 not invent the character's registration history. [1]
 Money, law-breaking and Russian interference
 The Electoral Commission found Vote Leave had exceeded its spending limit and
 breached reporting rules. It paid fines totalling GBP 61,000 in March 2019 and
 withdrew its appeal. A separate sanction on another campaigner was overturned
 on appeal. These distinctions matter. [4]

 The ISC's 2020 Russia report criticised the absence of a post-referendum
 assessment. In a ministerial answer on 15 October 2026, the Government
 acknowledged a serious Russian attempt to interfere, while stating it believed the
 attempts had not materially changed the outcome. That is an attributed official
 position, not proof of Russian control, vote-rigging or a particular politician's
 criminal motive. [5, 6]
 [1] UK Parliament: 2016 result, franchise and background
 [2] UK Supreme Court: [2017] UKSC 5, paragraphs 116-125
 [3] European Union (Notification of Withdrawal) Act 2017
 [4] Electoral Commission: investigation and appeal updates
 [5] Intelligence and Security Committee: 2020 press notice
 [6] Hansard: ministerial answer, 15 October 2026 (uncorrected)




BEFORE THE SILENCE                                                                    11

The person inside the politics                                                              AUTHOR'S NOTE




 He had a life.
 He still deserves one.
 This fictional chapter draws on an anonymous personal account. The dialogue,
 cast, locations and visual scenes are dramatic reconstructions. No real private
 person is identified. The racism and the visitor with gun photographs are
 presented as part of that account, not as findings against a named person or a
 claim about all construction workers.
 An unwanted return is an individual story
 The UK left the EU on 31 January 2020; the transition ended on 31 December
 2020. The Withdrawal Agreement protects qualifying British residents in Spain.
 Brexit did not automatically expel every British person or remove all existing
 residence rights. This character feels compelled to return amid a life unravelling;
 the comic does not assert a deportation order or decide his legal status. Nor does
 his fear of being judged speak for everyone in Europe. [7]

 UKIP belongs to the referendum-era background; Reform UK is a later name. The
 Electoral Commission approved the change from The Brexit Party to Reform UK in
 January 2021. The story compresses time and does not place the later party name
 in the 2016 campaign. [8]
 Work, injury and dignity
 “Forced manual labour” and “slavery” preserve his description of economic
 coercion and the loss of a workable choice. A legal finding of slavery or forced
 labour would require further evidence. The collapse, seizure, spinal compression
 and loss of motor control are reported experiences; their sequence does not
 establish a medical diagnosis or a cause. His wish for the suffering to end shows
 the depth of his distress. His need is for care, safety and a future.

 He deserves dignity whether or not he has qualifications, speaks several
 languages, earns wages or can play again. That is the human centre of this book.
 [7] Spanish Government: residence and Withdrawal Agreement
 [8] Electoral Commission: 2021 party-registration decisions


 Read in order: Before the Silence → A Moment of Quiet → A Place to Begin. The
 wider proposal is Population, Permission and Sustainability.

title: A Moment of Quiet
description: Pain, consent, care and political pressure bring the question closer: what does a person need in order to recover and choose freely?

readerPages.text:
A GRAPHIC PREQUEL




A MOMENT
 OF QUIET
 Before A Place to Begin

Before the noise                                                THE STORY



   Before the forms and the waiting, there was music.




                                  Spinal compression. Pain. Movements
                                  he cannot always control.




   I need treatment. And someone to hear me.




A MOMENT OF QUIET                                                       2

Two voices, one demand                                   THE STORY



   Far-left authoritarianism.      Agree with us. We know
                                   best.




   Far-right extremism.            Blame outsiders. Only we
                                   can protect you.




   Where is the part where you listen?




A MOMENT OF QUIET                                               3

What feeds the shouting                                     THE STORY



   Each uses the other's anger to recruit.




   He sees fear beneath the anger. Ego makes backing down
   feel like defeat.




   Your fear does not give you ownership of me.

A MOMENT OF QUIET                                                  4

Listen to the patient                                            THE STORY



   An opioid? Pregabalin?              Explain the risks.




                                 Pregabalin clouded my memory. I fear
                                 another bad reaction.




               Being disabled isn't being stupid. I won't consent
               without a review.

A MOMENT OF QUIET                                                       5

Relief behind a price                                          THE STORY



   Cannabis eased my pain.




                                    He describes relief. They hear a
                                    label.


   The NHS route is closed to me here.




   The private route has a price I cannot reach.

A MOMENT OF QUIET                                                      6

Follow the money                                      THE STORY



   UK, US, Israel... who owns the clinics? Who gets
   paid?




   Can we learn from countries that widened access?




   Is care about need, or ability to pay?




A MOMENT OF QUIET                                            7

A table, not a throne                                           THE STORY



               Accept our help. Follow our way.




   Can we just talk?                   I'm listening.




   We can disagree and still care for each other.




                                       The middle ground he seeks
                                       begins with listening.


A MOMENT OF QUIET                                                      8

What he can carry                                               THE STORY



   He sells what he can. Keeps the guitar.




   The future has shrunk to a            Where can I sleep and feel
   question.                             safe?


   A friend drives. He needs rest.




A MOMENT OF QUIET                                                      9

A moment of quiet                                   THE STORY



   A place to stop. A door he can close.




   No shouting. No demands.




               Safe enough to sleep. For tonight.


A MOMENT OF QUIET                                         10

Care, risk and access                                                       FACT NOTES




 This fictional prequel draws on an anonymous personal account. Its character
 describes symptoms, barriers and adverse effects. These scenes are not a medical
 record or a finding about any real clinician. His need to be heard is the centre of
 the story.
 Legal does not always mean accessible
 The UK allowed specialist prescribing of qualifying cannabis medicines from 1
 November 2018. NHS access remains limited; the NHS describes insufficient
 evidence to recommend cannabis medicines generally for long-term pain. Private
 prescribing is a separate payment route. A private offer does not show that the
 NHS is funding it. [1, 2]
 Experience, benefit and harm
 He reports relief from cannabis and memory problems with pregabalin. Cannabis
 can also cause harm; reported relief does not establish a cure for spinal
 compression. Pregabalin is used for nerve pain and other conditions; it is not an
 opioid. It can cause memory problems. MHRA warnings cover dependence,
 withdrawal and infrequent severe breathing problems, sometimes without opioids.
 [2, 3, 4]

 Opioids are a class of different medicines, not a synonym for heroin. No
 heroin/diamorphine prescription is identified here. Opioids can relieve severe pain,
 while prolonged use can cause dependence and addiction even at prescribed
 doses. Risks require individual assessment and informed discussion. Changes to
 ongoing medication need a prescriber-supported plan; abruptly stopping
 pregabalin can cause harm. [4, 5]
 Loss of movement needs assessment
 New or worsening weakness or loss of movement needs urgent medical
 assessment. Back pain with new bladder or bowel problems or numbness around
 the groin or bottom requires emergency assessment. Symptom relief does not
 remove spinal nerve compression. [6]
 [1] UK Government: specialist prescribing, 1 November 2018
 [2] NHS: medical cannabis and access
 [3] NHS: pregabalin and memory problems
 [3] NHS: what pregabalin is used for
 [4] MHRA: dependence and withdrawal warnings, January 2026
 [4] MHRA: pregabalin and severe breathing problems
 [5] MHRA: opioid medicines, dependence and addiction
 [6] NHS: spinal compression and emergency symptoms




A MOMENT OF QUIET                                                                   11

Dignity before obedience                                                                     AUTHOR'S NOTE




 Care without coercion.
 A safe place to rest.
 The factions are fictional. Their cycle of fear, ego and escalation is a dramatic
 interpretation of authoritarianism and extremism. It does not describe every
 person on the left or right. Here, the middle ground means listening, evidence,
 consent and equal dignity.
 A person remains a person
 Disability does not determine intelligence or worth. NHS guidance starts from a
 presumption that adults can decide about their own treatment. People may need
 support to understand or communicate; dignity does not depend on income, paid
 work or independent speech. [7]
 Ownership and public accountability
 Curaleaf documents a US-linked group with a UK clinic founded with NHS doctors.
 Kanabo's 2024 issuer report describes Treat It and its Israeli R&D subsidiary.
 These records establish business connections at stated dates; they do not prove
 improper NHS payments, corruption or a motive to harm. [8, 9]
 Learn from different rules
 Germany changed its rules to allow specified adult possession and cultivation,
 with restrictions. That is different from a right to a prescription, free care or
 importing medicines. The character asks why fair access remains out of reach for
 him. [10]
 [7] NHS: consent and decision-making capacity
 [8] Curaleaf: corporate structure and clinic history
 [9] Kanabo: issuer annual report, 30 April 2024
 [10] German Health Ministry: Cannabis Act questions


 His search continues in A Place to Begin, the graphic adaptation of Population,
 Permission and Sustainability.

title: A Place to Begin
description: A possible beginning: secure homes, useful work, working services, protected green space and a community people can freely join.

readerPages.text:
A GRAPHIC STORY



A PLACE
TO BEGIN
 Population, Permission
   and Sustainability

Somewhere to live                                              THE STORY



   The room has an address. It does not feel like a home.




   You need somewhere                    Where can I afford?
   quieter.




   Different lives. The same question: where can a future
   begin?




A PLACE TO BEGIN                                                      2

An invitation                                         THE STORY



   What if we built whole   Who gets to belong?
   places to live?




   People. All of us.       Move by choice. Get help to
                            begin.




   I used to play.          Then bring your guitar.




A PLACE TO BEGIN                                             3

Build a whole place                                              THE STORY



   A place I can actually stay.         A warm, quiet, accessible home
                                        is the beginning.




   Then the things a home needs: care, learning, food, work
   and transport.




   Funded. Staffed. Working.            Ready for every household.




A PLACE TO BEGIN                                                         4

Room to grow                                                 THE STORY



   Start with 5,000 people.        Then 10,000. 25,000.
                                   50,000.




   Reserve the future footprint.   Do we have to stop life
   Protect the green land beyond   growing?
   it.




   No birth quotas.                No forced moves.




A PLACE TO BEGIN                                                    5

Look after what sustains us                                        THE STORY



   Solar roofs. Storage.                Local capability. Shared
   Shared backup.                       support.




   Treat and test drinking water. Clean wastewater.




   Grow. Repair. Reuse.




                                        Care for land and water.


A PLACE TO BEGIN                                                          6

A stake in the future                                              THE STORY



   I don't have money to                 Affordable homes. Help to
   begin.                                begin.




   Different homes. Different budgets. Safe building choices
   suited to each site.




   I can teach.                          Room to create. To trade. To
                                         build.




A PLACE TO BEGIN                                                          7

Belonging without obedience                                    THE STORY



   I need help. And quiet.          Your life. Your choices.




   Accessible help. Open budgets.   A fair way to challenge
                                    decisions.




   The law must change too.




                                    Proposed: no planned
                                    homelessness.


A PLACE TO BEGIN                                                      8

Independent, together                                                THE STORY



   Daily needs close by. Specialist hospitals, colleges and
   services shared between places.




   Connect transport, communications and science. Protect
   privacy. Support one another when systems fail.




   Local choices. A shared                More people creating and
   national safety net.                   sharing prosperity.




A PLACE TO BEGIN                                                            9

A place to begin                                                THE STORY



   Care for the land, in our own       And rest when you need to.
   ways.




   Still in pain. Now with a future.   Will you play again
                                       tomorrow?




                                       A home. A choice. A tomorrow
   Yes.                                together.


A PLACE TO BEGIN                                                      10

What the story is built on                                            RESEARCH NOTES




 The people and events in this comic are fictional. They illustrate one possible
 future, informed by an anonymous personal account and the wider Green Tank
 proposal. This is a concept, not an approved development or a promise of a
 home.
 The two PLOS ONE studies
 The Pre-History of Urban Scaling (2014) studies ancient settlements in the
 Basin of Mexico. It examines patterns of population and space. Its historical
 examples include settlements above 100,000; it does not establish a universal
 ceiling.
 Read the study: doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0087902


 Constraining the population size estimates of the pre-Columbian
 Casarabe Culture of Amazonian Bolivia (2025) estimates 10,000-100,000
 people across a 5,020 km² region of multiple settlements. The discussion
 suggests the total probably reached no more than 50,000. This is not a
 single-city population limit.
 Read the study: doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0325104


 Archaeology needs careful reading. Radiocarbon dates help date
 occupation and activity; they do not directly count residents. Population
 estimates combine evidence with assumptions and uncertainty.
 50,000 is a design choice
 The proposal starts at 5,000 and reserves space and infrastructure for staged
 growth to 50,000. Research does not prove that this is an ideal or maximum
 city size. This is a planning framework, not a birth quota or an expulsion rule.
 Future changes need public review. The aim is a complete community,
 protected green space and voluntary movement, with no borders between
 settlements.
 Green space still has uses and rights
 Fields, gardens and golf courses are not automatically spare land. Habitat,
 productive soils, flood risk, water, access and existing rights need assessment.
 The earlier UK sketch could not fit everyone with a strict ten-mile gap between
 settlement edges. It was an illustration, not a siting plan.




A PLACE TO BEGIN                                                                    11

From an idea to a real choice                                                          FURTHER READING



 Rights and finance would need to change
 Owning land does not currently give an unrestricted right to live or build on it.
 UN human-rights treaties do not automatically grant UK planning permission.
 The paper proposes stronger housing protections, accessible decisions and
 safeguards against eviction into homelessness. Affordable entry, grants, loans
 and government-backed zero-deposit mortgages are proposals to evaluate, not
 guaranteed schemes.
 Local capability, shared responsibility
 The wider design retains the UK Treasury and pooled national finance, with
 transparent local budgets and fair support between communities. It includes
 independent living and care homes; arts, science and enterprise; civilian
 policing and national defence; and freedom to share community space without
 compulsory belief. More widely shared opportunity is intended to support
 higher, sustainable prosperity; the outcome would need testing.
 Homes can take different forms
 Modular and demountable homes, suitable non-concrete foundations, mobile
 dwellings, tree-supported concepts and floating communities widen the design
 options. Each needs site-specific safety, access and environmental checks.
 Marine stewardship means protecting water and recovering nutrients safely,
 not dumping food or sewage into the sea.
 Parts of the idea already exist
 Garden cities and Letchworth: planned towns, green surroundings and
 community benefit. Vauban, Freiburg: low-energy neighbourhood design and
 transport. Schoonschip, Amsterdam: a small floating community and shared
 energy. Champlain Housing Trust: shared-equity housing that preserves
 affordability. Each is a partial precedent, not proof of this whole system.
 Letchworth: letchworth.com/about-us/our-history/

 Vauban: freiburg.de/pb/208736.html

 Schoonschip: schoonschipamsterdam.org/en/

 Champlain: getahome.org/innovation/


 Read alongside: Population, Permission and Sustainability, 15 October 2026. The
 companion paper contains the full argument, legal distinctions, uncertainties,
 population-study register and source references.

 Concept: The Green Tank. Adaptation and lettering: AI-assisted. Illustrations: AI-generated. Fictional
 cast; no real personal names or likenesses. First graphic edition, October 2026.




A PLACE TO BEGIN                                                                                      12

title: It Never Had to Be This Way
description: An imagined warning branch explores what could be lost when inequality, failed care, conflict and environmental pressures compound. It is not a forecast.

readerPages.text:
A POSSIBLE FUTURE



IT NEVER HAD
      TO BE
THIS WAY
 A future we can still change

If the invitation never came                                     IMAGINED FUTURE



   Imagine a future in which the barriers remain. What follows
   is a warning, not a forecast.




   Appointments existed. Reaching one, waiting for one,
   affording the journey: another struggle.




   Rent rose. Care, food and warmth slipped out of reach.




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                                   2

Who owned the future?                                             IMAGINED FUTURE



   Rent. Interest. Fees. An ordinary wage left less room for an
   ordinary life.




   Some owners lived nearby. Some never visited. Decisions
   travelled farther than responsibility.




                                 Who collects the return? Who pays
                                 when things break?




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                                    3

A beginning kept out of reach                               IMAGINED FUTURE



   One day, this will be yours.        I need a life before then.




   Age did not decide who cared. Some people opened their
   doors. Others protected the price of every key.




                               The shared room shut. People met less.
                               Rumour filled the space.




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                              4

The land and the lock                                              IMAGINED FUTURE



   He asked for space to live and grow. The owner preferred to
   wait for a higher price.




                I can trial new methods. I need training, finance and
                a fair buyer.




   Aquaponics. Perennials. Healthy soil. Useful trials struggled
   for support while speculation still paid.




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                                     5

Deals above the rubble                                           IMAGINED FUTURE



   Leaders announced bargains. People living under attack
   waited for peace.




   Arms orders grew. Fuel still moved. Income could rise while
   families lost everything.




                              Governments changed. Contracts
                              renewed. The war outlived the promises.




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                                   6

When fear found uniforms                                      IMAGINED FUTURE



   Each faction promised protection in exchange for
   obedience. Fear made an enemy easier to see than a
   neighbour.




   In this dark branch, intimidation became organised armed
   conflict. This escalation was a choice, not a destiny.




                                  The clinic closed. The food van
                                  stopped. Each side blamed the other
                                  for the lives between them.




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                                7

A country arguing with itself                                 IMAGINED FUTURE



   Some sought independent Scotland or Wales in Europe.
   Others argued for Irish unity. These futures required
   consent and decisions.




   People had crossed these seas for centuries. No ancestry
   made today's neighbours worth less.




   Whichever constitution people chose, homes, care and
   opportunity still had to be built.




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                                8

The warnings became weather                                    IMAGINED FUTURE



   The world kept warming. Heat, flood and drought reached
   people with the least protection.




   Damage ate into budgets. Repairs, insurance and food cost
   more. Spare money bought time.




   Scientists warned of a weaker Atlantic overturning
   circulation (AMOC). Sharper change was a serious risk.




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                                 9

If the Atlantic changed                                      IMAGINED FUTURE



   This imagined future includes a severe AMOC disruption
   over decades, reaching a society already divided.




   Elsewhere, heat and disrupted rains continued. Regional
   cold did not freeze the whole planet.




   Cold became deadly where warm homes, reliable power
   and care had already failed.




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                              10

The walls could not care                                         IMAGINED FUTURE



   Years later, the house still held its wealth. The town that
   sustained it had emptied.




                              I can pay. Why is nobody coming?




   Money could not become a nurse, a repair crew, clean water
   or a harvest.




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                                  11

It never had to be this way                                     CHOICES STILL OPEN



   There had been people here. Hands. Skills. Families. Time.
   More value than the accounts had ever counted.




   The imagined ending stops here. Our choices are still open.




   A home. Care. A share. A place to disagree and still belong.




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                                    12

Evidence and the imagined future                                        RESEARCH NOTES




 Research and reporting checked to 16 October 2026. The story combines
 documented pressures with a deliberately severe fictional branch. It does not
 estimate the probability of that whole chain, establish secret motives, or predict
 the disappearance of humanity.
 Wealth, ownership and access
 ONS estimates for Great Britain in April 2020-March 2022 put the wealth of the
 richest 1% of households equal to that of the least wealthy 50% combined. This is
 a concentration measure, not evidence that inequality rises every year; pandemic
 survey and pension-method changes limit comparisons. [1]

 Overseas beneficiaries held 58.8% of the market value of UK quoted shares in
 2024. That is not a share of all UK land, GDP or money. Investment can build
 capacity; ownership data alone establish neither extraction nor wrongdoing. The
 story asks who benefits, who contributes and who answers for the costs. [2]
 Care can exist and remain hard to reach
 The October 2026 Commons briefing reports a waiting list below its 2023 peak,
 but persistent failure of the 18-week target. Doctor and nurse numbers rose over
 the five years to July 2026; counts do not adjust for demand. DHSC documents
 real medicine shortages and systems to manage them. Current evidence supports
 access problems, not a claim that doctors and medicines have vanished. [3, 4]
 War: events, interests and interpretation
 Reuters reported renewed strikes and the breakdown of an announced energy
 truce on 15 October. SIPRI records USD 679 billion in Top 100 arms revenues in
 2024: revenue is not profit or proof of a plan for endless war. Le Monde analysed
 the fuel deal as advantageous to Russia. The White House's 5 October diesel
 policy stressed affordability; senators opposed the Russian deal on 13 October.
 These are reported events, analysis and competing official positions. A shared
 scheme to prolong war for personal profit is not established here. [5-9]
 [1] ONS: household wealth, April 2020 to March 2022
 [2] ONS: ownership of UK quoted shares, 2024
 [3] Commons Library: NHS key statistics, 2 October 2026
 [4] DHSC: medicine supply management, 2026
 [5] Reuters: energy truce breaks down, 15 October 2026
 [6] SIPRI: Top 100 arms revenues, 2024 (released 2025)
 [7] Le Monde: fuel-deal analysis, 12-13 October 2026
 [8] White House: diesel-affordability policy, 5 October 2026
 [9] US senators: letter opposing diesel deal, 13 October 2026




IT NEVER HAD TO BE THIS WAY                                                           13

Land, food and a warming world                                          RESEARCH NOTES



 Land ownership is not the same as usable income
 England's 2024/25 farm accounts show wide differences between farm types and
 income sources. Many farms already diversify: 72% had diversified activity and
 27% generated solar energy. Land, debt, tenancy, unpaid family work and cash
 flow need separate examination. A field can be food production, habitat or flood
 storage. Neither acreage nor a quiet-looking field proves greed or uselessness.
 [10]

 The land investor, the hesitant owner and the farmer seeking support are fictional
 composites. Their different choices matter. No finding about a named farm, family
 or business is made.
 Aquaponics and perennials are real tools
 FAO's technical manual sets out integrated fish-and-plant production, system
 design, biological management and costs. Aquaponics needs expertise, reliable
 power, feed and water management; suitable yields do not remove those inputs. It
 can complement farming, rather than demonstrate that all fields, staple crops or
 tractors are redundant. [11]

 A perennial-rice field study found eight harvests from one planting over four years,
 with yields comparable to replanted annual rice and benefits to soil and labour
 inputs. It also identified adoption risks. This is evidence for innovation under the
 conditions tested, not proof that the same crop, yield or economics transfers to
 every UK site. Other perennial crops need their own local trials. [12]
 The climate baseline is still global warming
 UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2025 found that global greenhouse-gas emissions
 continued rising in 2024. It estimated about 2.8 °C of warming this century under
 the policies it assessed, compared with 2.3-2.5 °C if stated national commitments
 were fully implemented. Those are conditional global projections above
 pre-industrial levels, not a single local weather forecast or an unchangeable
 destiny. [13]

 The plot shows how housing, health, food, energy and climate shocks could
 compound. That interaction is the story's organising hypothesis; no cited study
 validates every link or proves that one settlement size would prevent the ending.
 [10] Defra: farm accounts, England, 2024/25
 [11] FAO: Small-scale aquaponic food production, 2014
 [12] Nature Sustainability: perennial rice field trials, 2022/23
 [13] UNEP: Emissions Gap Report 2025

AMOC: risk without a countdown                                      SCIENCE & UNCERTAINTY




 The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation transports heat through the ocean.
 It is a circulation system, not a switch that freezes the whole planet. Weakening,
 loss of northern deep-water formation and a complete overturning collapse are
 related questions that require clear definitions.
 Read the assumptions behind the headlines
 The IPCC's 2021 assessment expected AMOC weakening this century and
 expressed medium confidence that an abrupt collapse would not occur before
 2100. That is a dated assessment with stated uncertainty, not a guarantee. [14]

 A 2025 Nature study, also presented in an author-written EGU abstract, found
 persistent overturning in its model experiments under extreme forcing, identifying
 a stabilising role for Southern Ocean upwelling. It concluded that collapse this
 century was unlikely within that analysis. [15]

 A 2026 Science Advances study used observations to constrain model projections
 and estimated roughly 50% weakening by the end of the century. This raises
 concern about stronger change; it does not report an observed 50% fall today or
 establish a certain collapse date. The two studies use different questions and
 assumptions. Their headlines cannot be treated as a simple vote for safety or
 doom. [16]
 A stress scenario describes consequences if it happens
 The Met Office's high-impact, low-likelihood work includes conditional
 AMOC-collapse experiments with substantial UK cooling, changed rainfall and
 other impacts relative to a world without that collapse. The report's assumed start
 and peak dates are scenario inputs. They are not forecast dates. Climate effects
 differ by region; wider global warming and other hazards continue. [17]

 The comic chooses severe disruption as a fictional stress test over decades. It
 assigns no probability to that branch. It does not claim that AMOC collapse is
 inevitable, that Britain instantly becomes an ice sheet, or that humanity is
 scientifically expected to freeze to extinction. Serious uncertainty supports
 preparation, emissions cuts and resilient services; it does not require fatalism.

Voices, nations and belonging                                                 RESEARCH & AUTHOR'S NOTE



 A shared political space
 OECD's 2026 survey links perceived political voice with trust. This is not a civil-war
 forecast. MI5's October 2026 threat assessment documents serious extremist
 risks, including a rising extreme-right threat. It does not predict symmetrical
 left-right armies or inevitable UK civil war. Those factions and their escalation are
 fictional. [18, 19]
 Constitutional futures require choices and law
 An independent Scotland or Wales could seek EU membership through accession
 rules and agreement; membership is not automatic. Irish unity has a distinct
 consent-based route under the Belfast/Good Friday Agreement. The European
 Council recognised that a lawfully united Ireland would be in the EU. There is no
 procedure called the Celtic nations ejecting England. An eligible future English
 state could also seek EU membership. [20-22]
 History is migration, not inherited guilt
 A 2022 ancient-DNA study combined 460 genomes with archaeology and 57 new
 radiocarbon dates, finding substantial North Sea migration and later mixture.
 Anglo-Saxon settlement involved several kingdoms, not one simple arrival in
 Mercia. Ancestry neither ranks present-day rights nor makes descendants guilty.
 The story rejects exclusion, whichever nationality it targets. [23, 24]
